items.followUp: Name four common types of test data.

rubric.why: Any two correct test data types earn this mark.
rubric.description: Names two valid types of test data.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any two distinct correct types.

rubric.why: The question asks for four types in total.
rubric.description: Names the remaining two valid types.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark when four distinct correct types are named.

modelAnswer: Four types of test data are:
Normal data
Boundary data
Extreme data
Erroneous data.

items.followUp: What is a candidate solution to a problem?

rubric.why: A candid (candidate) solution is a possible or proposed way to solve a problem.
rubric.description: Identifies it as a possible or proposed solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it is a possible or proposed solution.

rubric.why: A proposed solution is checked to determine whether it appropriately solves the problem.
rubric.description: Explains that the solution is assessed for suitability or requirements.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for noting that it is tested or evaluated against the problem's requirements.

modelAnswer: A candid (candidate) solution is a possible solution proposed for a problem.
It is tested or evaluated to check whether it meets the problem's requirements.

items.followUp: What is a hyperlink, and how is one created in HTML?

rubric.why: A hyperlink provides a link from one resource or location to another.
rubric.description: States that a hyperlink links to another resource or location.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing it as a link or connection.

rubric.why: A hyperlink is typically activated by clicking linked text or an image.
rubric.description: Identifies a linked destination or its clickable form.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning a destination such as a webpage/document or clickable text/image; the HTML anchor tag is also acceptable.

modelAnswer: A hyperlink is a clickable text or image that connects to another webpage, document, or location.
In HTML, it is commonly created with the <a href="address"> anchor tag.

items.followUp: Write the output of this code: Computer Science

rubric.why: The browser displays the text contained between the body tags.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the output text.

rubric.why: The <b> tag displays its enclosed text in bold.
rubric.description: States that the output text is bold.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for noting the bold formatting.

modelAnswer: He is my Son is displayed in bold.

items.followUp: Define a simple proposition and give one example of a compound proposition.

rubric.why: A compound proposition is formed by combining propositions.
rubric.description: States that it is made by combining two or more propositions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct formation.

rubric.why: Logical connectives are used to combine simple propositions.
rubric.description: Names a connective or gives a valid connective-based example.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying a logical connective or giving an example such as p AND q.

modelAnswer: A compound proposition is formed by combining two or more simple propositions using logical connectives.
For example, “It is raining AND it is cold” is a compound proposition.

items.followUp: Name the two main categories of computer memory.

rubric.why: Primary (main) memory is one main category of computer memory.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for primary or main memory.

rubric.why: Secondary (auxiliary) memory is the other main category.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for secondary or auxiliary memory.

modelAnswer: The two main types of computer memory are:
Primary memory
Secondary memory.

items.followUp: What digits are used in the binary number system, and what is its base?

rubric.why: The binary system has base two.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the base is 2.

rubric.why: Binary numbers use only the digits 0 and 1.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving both 0 and 1.

modelAnswer: The binary number system has base 2.
It uses only the digits 0 and 1.

rubric.why: Dividing 156 by 16 gives quotient 9 and remainder 12, and hexadecimal digit 12 is C.
rubric.description: Shows the correct quotient and hexadecimal remainder/digit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct division result and conversion of remainder 12 to C.

rubric.why: Reading the hexadecimal digits from quotient to remainder gives 9C.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the final answer 9C₁₆.

modelAnswer: Given: (156)₁₀
Divide by 16: 156 ÷ 16 = 9 remainder 12.
In hexadecimal, 12 = C.
Read the quotient and remainder in order: (156)₁₀ = (9C)₁₆.
